newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-PITINO LEAVING UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY FOR BOSTON CELTICS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-PITINO LEAVING UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY FOR BOSTON CELTICS.

text.p: Rick Pitino left one traditional basketball power for another, stepping down Tuesday as coach of the University of Kentucky to take control of the NBA's floundering Boston Celtics.
After building Kentucky up from the disarray of an NCAA probation into a national champion, Pitino said he was leaving Lexington for Boston, where he got his start in coaching.

"It is a similar type of situation at the professional level that I had eight years ago at this level," Pitino said at an emotional news conference on the Kentucky campus. "That's what I want to do, more than anything else ... It's a monster challenge."
Various reports indicate Pitino will receive a 10-year deal worth an astonishing $70 million and will serve as director of operations as well as coach of the Celtics.
"It's not about money," said Pitino, who becomes the best-paid NBA coach with this deal. "At this stage of my life, it's not the money. I love the challenge."
Pitino, who succeeds M.L. Carr as Boston coach, faces a massive renovation with the Celtics, who are coming off the worst season (15-67) in the storied history of the franchise.
"Rick Pitino is a great coach," Celtics president Red Auerbach said in a television interview Tuesday with CNN/SI.
"Anytime you get a great coach you know you are going to improve your position. He's a great coach, he's proven that, there's no question. He's a great motivator."

Pitino said he spoke with his Kentucky players Sunday and made the decision to leave Monday night, although he admitted he "waffled back and forth" over the last two days. He met Tuesday with Kentucky athletic director C.M. Newton prior to the news conference.
"C.M. and I both feel we built a model for integrity and compliance," Pitino said. "We built something we could be proud of. It starts with the foundation. Nothing is going to wash this house away."
After winning the NCAA title in 1996, Pitino turned down similar deals from the Celtics and New Jersey Nets. He also was courted this year by Orlando and Philadelphia.
But he chose the rich tradition of the Celtics, who have won 16 NBA championships but none since 1986.
Pitino described the Celtics as "full of glory, tradition and pride and I'd like to see them get back to that championship level."

Pitino said he is bringing Kentucky assistants Jim O'Brien and Winston Bennett with him to Boston, where he began his career as coach of Boston University 19 years ago, making a name for himself as someone who can quickly turn around a team's fortunes.

Boston University won 17 games over two seasons before Pitino's arrival and 17 games in its first season with him. Providence University won 11 games before Pitino arrived in 1985 and was in the Final Four two years later.

Pitino used that as a springboard to the coaching job of the New York Knicks where he turned a moribund franchise into a division winner in two years. He went 90-74 but feuded with general manager Al Bianchi and left for Kentucky.
When Pitino arrived in Lexington in 1989, the Wildcats had been ravaged by probation. Pitino responded by guiding them to a 14-14 season and returned Kentucky to national prominence one year later.

After Final Four trips in 1993 and 1995, Pitino and Kentucky won the national title in 1996 and nearly repeated this year, losing to Arizona in the championship game. He has a career college mark of 352-124.
